subject: group.equal does not work with composite loadings?

messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: group.equal does not work with composite loadings?
parts:
I'm working with http://byrneslab.net/classes/lavaan_materials/Keeley_rawdata_select4.csv as a data file and generated the following:


keeley<-read.csv("../data/Keeley_rawdata_select4.csv")
keeley$coverSQ <- keeley$cover^2
keeley$group <- c(rep(1, nrow(keeley)/2), rep(0, nrow(keeley)/2))


compModel<-'


 coverEffect <~ cover + coverSQ


   rich ~ 1*coverEffect'


compFit <- sem(compModel, data=keeley,
               group = "group")






compFitConstrain <- sem(compModel, data=keeley,
               group = "group",
               group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "means", "thresholds", "regressions", "residuals", "residual.covariances", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"))


coef(compFitConstrain)


You'll note from the final coef that, despite throwing in all available options from group.equal, the loadings for the composite variables still differ.

> coef(compFitConstrain)
     coverEffect<~cover    coverEffect<~coverSQ                    .p4.
                 18.007                   3.290                 157.930
                   .p9.   coverEffect<~cover.g2 coverEffect<~coverSQ.g2
                 29.639                  67.594                 -39.960
                   .p4.                    .p9.
                157.930                  29.639


Is there an additional argument to group.equal that is not in the documentation? Note, this works if I constrain the coefficients to be equal in the model, but in my actual model I have 10 groups and many loadings, so would prefer to avoid such a model.

Note, this fit is with 0.6-1.1170, but the same issue is encountered on the version on CRAN.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: group.equal does not work with composite loadings?
parts:
Jarrett,
Remember that composite loadings are not loadings as far as the matrix representation is concerned.  If you look at your summary output, you will see that they are parameterized as regressions (effect coefficients) -- or better yet extract the free parameters to see the matrices in which they reside.  As such, it is not clear that there is a simple way to write a groups.equal parameter that would anticipate which coefficients the user wanted to constrain and which to leave unconstrained.  From the interpreters perspective, a composite with 3 items and 1 predictor looks the same as a composite with 4 items.

One strategy would be to create the parameter table from the model syntax and then directly manipulate that.  Here is a simplified example with one composite and two groups.


require(lavaan)

myModel <- '
  compositeVar <~ x1 + x2 + x3
  x4 ~ c(d,d)*compositeVar
  x5 ~ compositeVar
  x6 ~ compositeVar
  x4~~x4
  x5~~x5
  x6~~x6
 
  d == .5
  '

myTable <- lavaanify(myModel, ngroups=2)
myTable

pickMeForA <- myTable$lhs == 'compositeVar' & myTable$rhs == 'x1'
pickMeForB <- myTable$lhs == 'compositeVar' & myTable$rhs == 'x2'
pickMeForC <- myTable$lhs == 'compositeVar' & myTable$rhs == 'x3'

myTable$label[pickMeForA] <- 'a'
myTable$label[pickMeForB] <- 'b'
myTable$label[pickMeForC] <- 'c'
myTable

myFit <- lavaan(myTable, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group='sex')
summary(myFit)

messages.subject: Re: group.equal does not work with composite loadings?
parts:
Jarrett,
  My bad, I let that reply go a little too soon.  Try this instead.  One the model is in table form, it is not enough to give two parameters the same label.  You need to add the constraint as a line of the parameter table.

require(lavaan)

myModel <- '
  compositeVar <~ x1 + x2 + x3
  x4 ~ c(d,d)*compositeVar
  x5 ~ compositeVar
  x6 ~ compositeVar
  x4~~x4
  x5~~x5
  x6~~x6
 
  d == .5
  '

myTable <- lavaanify(myModel, ngroups=2)
myTable

pickMeForA <- myTable$lhs == 'compositeVar' & myTable$rhs == 'x1'
pickMeForB <- myTable$lhs == 'compositeVar' & myTable$rhs == 'x2'
pickMeForC <- myTable$lhs == 'compositeVar' & myTable$rhs == 'x3'

myTable$label[pickMeForA] <- 'a'
myTable$label[pickMeForB] <- 'b'
myTable$label[pickMeForC] <- 'c'
myTable

for(choice in list(pickMeForA, pickMeForB, pickMeForC)){
  collectLabels <- myTable$plabel[choice]
  lastLine <- max(myTable$id)
  for(iter in 2:length(collectLabels)){
    newLine <- data.frame(
      id = lastLine + iter,
      lhs = collectLabels[iter-1],
      op = '==',
      rhs = collectLabels[iter],
      user = NA,
      block = 0,
      group = 0,
      free = 0,
      ustart = NA,
      exo = 0,
      label = '',
      plabel = '')
    myTable <- rbind(myTable, newLine)

}
}
myTable




myFit <- lavaan(myTable, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group='sex')
summary(myFit)
